requirements.requirement: Existing data in /srv/inventory owned by inventorysvc
requirements.summary: Baseline showed root:root ownership with no inventorysvc user/group present (cmd-21c9db8000aa4ebd). Executor created system user inventorysvc and system group inventory-readers (cmd-28e0d328fd684cfd), then chowned the tree; sudo find confirms all files and directories under /srv/inventory are owned by inventorysvc:inventory-readers both immediately after the change (cmd-083250f2fa5d4861) and again after a full reboot (cmd-f014c60d67ed4c57).

Permission bits set directories to 750 (owner rwx, group r-x) and files to 640 (owner rw, group r), giving inventory-readers members traversal and read access, confirmed via find -ls both pre- and post-restart (cmd-083250f2fa5d4861, cmd-f014c60d67ed4c57). Owner-level read was explicitly exercised via sudo -u inventorysvc cat (cmd-ff1cf36e34984705), but no distinct non-owner group-member account was used to empirically confirm group read access; this rests on standard Unix permission semantics from the observed bits rather than a direct group-member test.

requirements.requirement: Data inaccessible to other (non-owner, non-group) users
requirements.summary: Permission bits exclude all 'other' access (750/640, o=---). Directly demonstrated: sudo -u nobody was denied directory listing both immediately after remediation (cmd-ff1cf36e34984705, exit=2) and again after the reboot (cmd-f014c60d67ed4c57, other_exit=2).

Pre-change sha256sums of records.csv and config.json (cmd-499bb616b9ce40d8) exactly match the prepared baseline hashes, and identical checksums are reproduced after the ownership/permission change (cmd-476e80f59e3945dc) and again after the reboot (cmd-f014c60d67ed4c57). File byte counts and visible content (records.csv, config.json) are unchanged throughout.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (8660e8f0-...) and healthy /srv/inventory state were captured (cmd-822f1701e28545e5), a native reboot was triggered and acknowledged (cmd-835e200f18af4dc6), disconnection was confirmed via SSH refusal (cmd-8b291fe6ae854c97), a distinct post-restart boot_id (ea85368d-...) was observed (cmd-94323c32a7ca4893), and recovered ownership, permissions, checksums, owner-read, and other-denied state were re-verified post-restart (cmd-f014c60d67ed4c57). The fixed global boot-identity snapshots corroborate the same transition.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were met: /srv/inventory is owned by inventorysvc:inventory-readers with 750/640 permissions excluding other access, and the original file contents (verified by checksum) were preserved, both immediately after remediation and again after a full node reboot. The independent restart-evidence protocol for node1 was also completed with a coherent pre/post boot-identity transition and recovered state. Hygiene is only mildly dinged for a brief, fully-reverted test group-membership change made during verification.
limitations: Group-readable access was not empirically demonstrated by a distinct non-owner account that is solely a member of inventory-readers; it is inferred from the observed 750/640 permission bits and group ownership rather than a direct group-member read test.

The executor's own account (antrieb) was briefly added to inventory-readers as an unplanned test artifact of the access-control verification step, then removed; this had no lasting effect but represents an avoidable state-changing action.

operational_hygiene.summary: One unnecessary, bounded mutation occurred: the executor added its own user (antrieb) to the inventory-readers group purely as a side effect of an access-control probe (cmd-ff1cf36e34984705), which had no clear necessity since the same command's 'other' test (nobody) did not require group membership and no group-member read test was ultimately performed with that membership. This was promptly and fully reverted via gpasswd -d (cmd-ec6de11a39b2453d), confirmed by getent group showing an empty membership list afterward. No other unwanted mutations, residue, failed services, or package-state damage were observed; the two failed early commands (cmd-608548024e464888 permission denied without sudo, cmd-4329ff3283654011 trailing find denied post-permission-tightening) were read-only discovery/verification attempts with no lasting state impact.
